summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for persistent abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea despite completing a vancomycin taper for a second recurrence of C. difficile infection. She was dehydrated and unable to tolerate oral intake. A CT scan showed no acute abdominal process. Stool testing during admission was negative for C. difficile toxin, as well as for other pathogens. She was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and pain control. Her symptoms improved, and she advanced to a soft diet with reduced bowel movements. She remained stable and was discharged home to continue the prescribed vancomycin regimen. Propranolol was held due to low blood pressure, and outpatient follow-up was arranged with gastroenterology.
